reports.title: Mandeep Singh
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: the Trust has undertaken initiatives to seek to educate both the public in relation to the appropriateness of making calls and to work with colleagues in other sectors to try to reduce the demand on Trust services.
promises.summary: Educate public and collaborate with other sectors to reduce demand

concerns.quote: severe demand and shortages in the division
Road closures and diversions did not assist the crews

reports.title: Maureen Wharton
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: No enquiry was made of Maureen as to the nature of her location and the potential support or assistance readily at hand or otherwise.
concerns.hazard: lack of inquiry into location and support

concerns.quote: No further enquiries were made to identify familial or social support which might or could have been enlisted or alerted to her presenting danger
concerns.hazard: failure to identify familial or social support

concerns.quote: No NEAS protocol appears to exist to assist personnel to initiate a response other than one limited to and directing an ambulance allocation
concerns.hazard: absence of protocol for non-ambulance response

concerns.quote: No working arrangement appears to exist to enlist the aid of other Agencies to support the patient or react more directly and in timely way to monitor and evaluate the nature of the presenting danger
a period of 3.45 hours elapsed between the first call and the arrival of an Ambulance crew at Maureen's side

reports.title: Donna Smith: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The call handler did not detect a worsening condition and did not escalate the call from Category 2 to category 1.
The methods of detecting worsening conditions in existing category 2 calls are not sufficiently robust (dispatch clinician and numerous call condition).
The category 2 call target (18minute average response and 95th percentile a 40minute response) was breached and the ambulance arrived 1 hour and 6 minutes after the first call.

links.explanation: Both reports identify delays in ambulance response times as a safety concern. The earlier report attributes delays to high demand and staffing shortages, while the later report cites inadequate detection of worsening conditions by call handlers.
links.earlier_quote: the reasons for the delay of the ambulance arrival include severe demand and shortages in the division.
links.later_quote: The call handler did not detect a worsening condition and did not escalate the call from Category 2 to category 1.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in recognizing the urgency of a patient's condition, leading to delayed ambulance response. The earlier case involved missed evaluation of information during the call, while the later case concerned inadequate detection of worsening conditions and lack of call escalation.
links.earlier_quote: Central to these concerns are that a period of 3.45 hours elapsed between the first call and the arrival of an Ambulance crew at Maureen's side.
